title: Cross-provider REFER transfer continuity and accessibility readiness
objective: Turn ACE Direct transfer behavior into a provider-neutral interoperability scenario that binds the original dialog, REFER transaction, NOTIFY outcome, replacement dialog, referred target identity, and post-transfer accessibility readiness without treating signaling success as a usable handoff.

historicalBasis.observation: ACE Direct routes transfer requests through JsSIP RTCSession.refer(), records REFER subscribers by transaction identity, distinguishes blind versus warm transfer state at the application layer, and hands multiparty host responsibility to a backup agent before the old host terminates its leg.
historicalBasis.scope: Motivating interoperability evidence only. Provider A/B/C identities are synthetic placeholders. Baudot does not infer any behavior of a contemporary VRS provider from the ACE donor or from the deterministic reducer.

providerModel.directions: all ordered pairs where source != target
providerModel.rule: provider identity is configuration, never implementation semantics

assertions: REFER acceptance does not imply a replacement dialog was established
successful NOTIFY status does not imply the replacement leg is accessibility-ready
the replacement dialog must bind to the intended referred target identity
a continuity-preserving transfer must not terminate the old leg before the configured replacement-leg readiness point
provider labels do not alter readiness semantics

proves: all directed provider pairs are represented independently of provider implementation
blind and warm transfer modes remain separate matrix dimensions
REFER acceptance, NOTIFY outcome, replacement-dialog establishment, target correlation, old-leg teardown, and RTT readiness reduce as separate facts
signaling-only transfer success cannot produce an accessibility-ready verdict
premature old-leg teardown is distinguishable from signaling and accessibility failure
replacement-target drift is distinguishable from signaling success
doesNotProve: live SIP REFER or NOTIFY exchange

requiredBeforeRunnable: live JAIN SIP REFER and NOTIFY execution adapter on an established dialog
at least two independently addressed provider-role endpoints with preserved original and replacement dialog identities
raw REFER, NOTIFY, replacement INVITE, response, and teardown evidence
independent RTT or media readiness observation on the replacement leg
terminal reduction that joins transfer signaling, target correlation, continuity, and accessibility readiness without collapsing them
requiredBeforeProven: repeatable execution across more than one SIP implementation
all configured provider directions exercised without provider-specific changes to the reducer
blind and warm transfer coverage with standards-grounded handling of any Replaces usage
failure evidence for rejected REFER, failed NOTIFY outcome, target mismatch, premature teardown, and accessibility-readiness loss
production-representative gateway or VRS observations without weakening claim boundaries

doesNotEstablish: that any named or unnamed provider supports REFER
that ACE Direct transfer behavior is defective or normative
